jobs.title: Director, Strategic Asset Allocation
jobs.description:
At Equitable, we believe work should be a place where you feel supported, inspired, and empowered to grow. In our caring and collaborative environment, your curiosity is encouraged, your passion is recognized, and your contributions truly matter. Together, we create meaningful impact, for our clients, our communities, and each other.

The Opportunity:
  At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

Join Equitable’s Strategic Asset Allocation team and play a key role in shaping the long-term investment strategy of the General Fund. In this role, you will lead the development, implementation, and communication of strategic asset allocation and portfolio initiatives, integrating investment, liability, capital, liquidity, risk, and financial performance considerations into actionable recommendations. Working closely with leaders across Asset Management, Finance, Actuarial, Risk, Product, and Technology, you will provide executive-ready insights that support financial strength, product competitiveness, capital efficiency, and sustainable growth. This is a highly visible opportunity to influence strategic decision-making, strengthen asset allocation capabilities, and contribute to the organization’s long-term success.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements:
This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.

Reports To:
AVP, Portfolio Risks & ALM

Department:
Asset Management

Term:
Permanent Full-Time

What you’ll do:

Lead the development and maintenance of General Fund portfolio strategies that balance financial objectives, risk appetite, regulatory considerations, and long-term business goals
Develop strategic asset allocation recommendations using quantitative analysis, insurance liability insights, and asset-liability management principles to enhance policyholder value and capital efficiency
Create and enhance analytical frameworks that support investment decision-making, portfolio monitoring, performance evaluation, and relative value assessments
Manage quarterly reporting and analysis of IFRS Net Investment Results, providing clear insights on portfolio performance, market developments, and key drivers of results
Develop and utilize modelling and risk management tools to assess interest rate, equity, credit, liquidity, and other investment risks while supporting asset-liability risk management activities
Partner with Finance, Actuarial, Product, Risk, and Asset Management teams on strategic initiatives, capital allocation decisions, product development, financial planning, and business strategy
Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and governance committees by delivering executive-ready recommendations, investment analysis, and strategic insights
Identify, assess, and manage operational risks related to analytical models, data, methodologies, reporting processes, and decision-support frameworks while maintaining strong governance, controls, and documentation practices

What you’ll bring:

Post-secondary degree in Actuarial Science, Commerce, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, Finance, or a related quantitative discipline
FSA/FCIA designation
Experience in portfolio management, asset-liability management, insurance investment strategy, financial modelling, capital management, risk management, or investment performance analysis
Strong understanding of fixed income, private credit, mortgages, real estate, equities, derivatives, liquidity management, and liability-driven investment strategies
Proven ability to develop quantitative models, optimization frameworks, scenario analysis, risk dashboards, governance materials, and executive-ready recommendations
Demonstrated ability to build strong relationships and influence stakeholders across Asset Management, Finance, Actuarial, Risk, Product, and Technology functions
Strong documentation, governance, and continuous improvement skills, with experience developing scalable processes, policies, guidelines, controls, and reporting practices
Experience with Python, R, SQL, VBA, Power BI, or similar analytical and automation tools is considered an asset

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities 
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching 
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year
Flexibility: Healthy work-life balance with employee wellness always top of mind, complemented by a “dress for your day” approach

We’re committed to fair pay and an inclusive, accessible hiring experience. If you need accommodations or alternative formats at any stage, just reach out to us at careers@equitable.ca. We’re happy to help.

If you’re selected to move forward, our Talent Acquisition team will walk you through all the details of our total rewards program, so you know exactly what’s included. This position is open and we are excited to find the right person to join our team. Your base pay will be based on your skills, qualifications, experience and education.

At Equitable, your resume will be reviewed by real people and all hiring decisions are made by our recruiters and hiring managers. AI tools may be used to support administrative and productivity tasks throughout the recruitment process, but we believe that evaluating experience, skills, and talent potential requires meaningful human interaction.

As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure and trusted workplace, candidates selected to move forward in the recruitment process will be required to complete a background screening in accordance with company policy.

jobs.title: Head, HR Operations, Transformation & Service Delivery
jobs.description:
Imagine working at the forefront of innovation in fluid-flow technology, with over 1,600 colleagues across the globe, and contributing to a legacy of excellence that spans eight manufacturing facilities on four continents. Armstrong Fluid Technology is more than just a leader in our industry; we are a community of the brightest and most creative minds, driven by a shared mission to engineer the future and safeguard our planet.

The Head, HR Operations, Transformation & Service Delivery provides enterprise leadership for the design, delivery and continuous improvement of Armstrong's HR operations and service delivery model. The role is accountable for creating a simple, scalable, employee-centered and operationally disciplined HR environment, ensuring that core HR services are delivered consistently, efficiently and with clear ownership across the employee lifecycle.

Leading HR Operations, HR transformation, process excellence and service delivery, the role translates people strategy into practical operating models, standardized processes, service standards and measurable business outcomes.

A core mandate is to continuously challenge how work is performed through simplification to improvement philosophy, ensuring technology enables well-designed processes rather than automating unnecessary complexity.

Key Accountabilities

HR Operations & Service Delivery
Lead Armstrong's enterprise HR Operations and service delivery capability, establishing clear service ownership, operating standards, controls and performance expectations.
Establish consistent processes across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, employee changes, transfers, promotions, leaves, organizational changes and offboarding.
Define and maintain HR service levels, escalation protocols, service ownership and operational performance measures.
Establish HR knowledge management standards, ensuring employees, managers and HR teams have access to accurate and current policies, procedures and guidance.
Build operational controls that strengthen compliance, data integrity, documentation quality and execution consistency.
Identify recurring service issues and resolve root causes rather than relying on manual workarounds.
Develop dashboards and performance reviews covering transaction quality, service volume, turnaround time, SLA achievement, employee experience and process effectiveness.
HR Transformation
Lead the enterprise HR transformation portfolio, translating strategic people priorities into structured programs, projects and implementation roadmaps.
Establish disciplined transformation governance including scope, objectives, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, risks, resource requirements and decision rights.
Manage cross-functional HR transformation initiatives from concept through design, implementation, stabilization and benefits realization.
Maintain an integrated transformation roadmap identifying interdependencies across people, process, technology, data and organizational change.
Establish portfolio prioritization methods ensuring HR resources are focused on initiatives delivering the highest organizational and employee value.
Provide clear executive-level reporting covering milestones, outcomes, risks, decisions, capacity and transformation benefits.
Ensure transformation initiatives transition effectively into sustainable business-as-usual ownership following implementation.
HR Process Excellence & Continuous Improvement
Establish the enterprise methodology for HR process design, documentation and continuous improvement.
Lead end-to-end process reviews across the employee lifecycle.
Facilitate current-state assessment, process mapping, root-cause analysis, requirements definition and future-state design.
Apply lean, continuous-improvement and structured problem-solving principles where appropriate.
Eliminate unnecessary handoffs, duplicative activities, manual intervention and unclear ownership.
Establish standard work, operating procedures, process controls, decision rights and performance measures.
Create and maintain an enterprise HR process catalogue identifying process owners and supporting technology.
Develop an HR continuous-improvement pipeline using employee feedback, service data, operational metrics and business requirements.
Partner with HR Technology & Data to determine where workflow automation, system optimization, AI or self-service can eliminate administrative work and improve service.
HR Service Delivery Model & Operating Model
Define which activities should be centralized, standardized, automated, delivered regionally or remain within specialist COEs.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, handoffs and escalation points.
Develop service catalogues and service-level expectations.
Establish appropriate governance between enterprise People & Organizational Capability teams and regional HR.
Reduce role ambiguity and duplicate activity across HR.
Ensure HRBP capacity is increasingly directed toward business partnership rather than transactional administration.
Establish scalable service models capable of supporting future organizational growth.
Change Management & Adoption
Embed structured change management into major HR transformation initiatives.
Develop stakeholder, communications, training, readiness and adoption plans appropriate to each initiative.
Assess organizational readiness and identify adoption barriers before implementation.
Equip managers and HR teams to successfully implement new policies, processes, systems and ways of working.
Establish adoption measures and monitor whether implemented changes are delivering intended outcomes.
Reinforce new ways of working through governance, measurement, leadership accountability and ongoing improvement.
Capture lessons learned and incorporate them into future transformation programs.
Digital Enablement & Partnership with HR Technology
Define business requirements and future-state process requirements.
Identify automation and digital workflow opportunities.
Establish process priorities for system improvements.
Participate in technology investment and enhancement prioritization.
Support testing, implementation, change readiness and adoption.
Ensure technology solutions support efficient processes and meaningful employee/manager experiences.
Partner on data-quality improvements arising from process or operating-model issues.
Governance, Risk & Controls
Establish appropriate operational governance across HR services and processes.
Maintain clear process ownership, decision rights and approval authorities.
Ensure HR operational practices comply with applicable organizational policies, employment requirements, privacy expectations and internal controls.
Partner with Legal, Finance, IT and other control functions where required.
Establish issue-management and escalation processes for material employee-service or operational risks.
Ensure documented procedures and controls remain current as processes, systems and organizational structures change.
Lead periodic reviews of HR operating effectiveness and identify required corrective actions.
Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership
Build and lead a high-performing HR Operations and Transformation capability.
Establish clear priorities, accountability and development expectations for the team.
Partner closely with HR Business Partners and People COEs to improve end-to-end delivery.
Serve as a trusted advisor on HR transformation, operating model and process effectiveness.
Facilitate decision-making across stakeholders with competing priorities.
Translate complex operational challenges into clear options, decisions and implementation plans.
Develop organizational capability in process thinking, continuous improvement, program management and change leadership.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, curiosity, simplification and evidence-based decision-making.

Role Requirements

University degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, Business Transformation or a related discipline.
CHRP/CHRL, PMP, PROSCI, Lean Six Sigma or comparable professional certification is an asset.
Typically,10–15+ years of progressive HR, transformation, operations, shared services, program management or process-improvement experience.
Significant experience leading complex HR transformation initiatives across functions and geographies.
Demonstrated experience designing or improving HR service delivery and operating models.
Strong understanding of employee lifecycle processes and HR operational controls.
Experience with HRIS platforms, workflow automation, digital HR and employee/manager self-service.
Demonstrated program and portfolio management capability.
Strong process design, continuous-improvement and problem-solving skills.
Experience establishing governance, performance measures and service standards.
Demonstrated change-management and organizational adoption experience.
Strong executive communication, facilitation and stakeholder-management capabilities.
Ability to translate strategy into practical and sustainable operating solutions.
Experience working across HR, IT, Finance, Legal and business functions in a complex or global organization.

Serve as a senior technology leader and trusted advisor to the Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer and Executive Team on cyber security, significant incidents, emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and security program developments

Establish and maintain information security policies, standards, procedures, controls, metrics, and performance indicators, driving continuous improvement in the organization’s security capabilities and maturity
Lead security operations, threat monitoring, vulnerability management, cyber resilience, incident response, recovery, post-incident remediation, and the oversight of security service providers and critical technology assets
Oversee security architecture, identity and access management, data protection, cloud and endpoint security, ensuring appropriate controls are integrated into technology solutions, projects, and business processes
Partner with business and technology leaders to enable secure innovation and digital transformation, provide security guidance for strategic initiatives and new capabilities, and support operational resilience and business continuity
Lead security awareness and training across the organization, promoting a security-first mindset and fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, resilience, and risk awareness
Manage technology vendor and third-party security assessments while maintaining effective relationships with security vendors, managed security service providers, industry and regulatory bodies, external advisors, and peer security leaders within the financial services industry

What you’ll bring:

Deep technical knowledge of enterprise security architecture, including zero trust, network segmentation, secure-by-design principles, defence-in-depth, secure software development, DevSecOps, application security testing, and API security
Strong understanding of hybrid and multi-cloud environments, cloud security posture management, and security across SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS platforms, with the ability to assess the security implications of core insurance and wealth platforms, legacy systems, and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled solutions
Extensive experience with SIEM, endpoint detection and response, and 24x7 security monitoring models, including managed security service providers, along with vulnerability and patch management, threat intelligence, penetration testing, and red/purple team practices
Proven ability to lead cyber incident response, crisis management, forensics, and recovery activities, including ransomware and third-party breach scenarios, with a strong understanding of disaster recovery, backup integrity, and operational resilience for critical business services
Deep knowledge of identity governance, privileged access management, multifactor authentication, single sign-on, conditional access, identity lifecycle controls, access certification, segregation of duties, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud and legacy environments
Strong knowledge of data discovery and classification, data loss prevention, encryption in transit and at rest, and cryptographic key, certificate, and secrets management, including controls protecting sensitive information shared with third parties or used by AI-enabled solutions
Demonstrated ability to challenge security designs and assessment findings, validate control effectiveness through technical evidence, and prioritize remediation based on exploitability, risk, and business impact
Experience evaluating security technologies and service providers for effectiveness, integration, operational complexity, and total cost of ownership, with the ability to translate technical gaps into prioritized security roadmaps with measurable outcomes, funding requirements, and the skills and resources required for delivery

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Services
jobs.description:
About Gowling Wlg

At Gowling WLG, our commitment to excellence begins with our people. As an international law firm with offices in Canada, the U.K., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, we’re proud to recruit and retain top talent who bring energy, insight, and a singular focus on delivering exceptional experiences – for our clients and each other.

We’re intentional about building a workplace that’s both high-performing and supportive, ensuring that everyone is empowered to do their best work and reach their full potential. Our culture is grounded in our shared values: Raise the Bar, Embrace Differences, and Thrive Together. These values shape how we collaborate, lead, and succeed – across teams, time zones, and career paths.

Whether you’re pursuing a role in law or business services, explore what’s possible and make your mark with Gowling WLG.

PROFILE

The Director, Corporate Services is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the delivery of corporate services across all Gowling WLG offices nationally. This role provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure consistent, high‑quality, and efficient support for the Firm’s Corporate professionals and clients. You will lead national teams, drive process standardization, oversee enabling technologies, and partner with key stakeholders to continuously improve service delivery, client experience, and operational performance.

This position can be based in our Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Hamilton, Waterloo or Ottawa office.

Responsibilities

Directs the efforts of the national Corporate Services team, including the development and implementation of strategies aligned with the Firm’s business goals to enhance corporate services delivery in all provinces in which the Firm operates.
Directs and enables development of an integrated team culture, vision and mission that drives effective interoffice collaboration, resource allocation and work sharing.
Ensures consistent application of standardized workflows, procedures, and precedents across all jurisdictions which the Firm operates, and subject to local requirements.
Provides senior oversight and strategic guidance on the selection, configuration and ongoing operation of corporate services technology platforms.
Partners with IT, Innovation, Knowledge & Practice Support, Finance, and Corporate leadership on technology, automation, precedents, and process improvement initiatives.
Responsible for ensuring effective and consistent onboarding, training, and continuous development programs for Corporate Services team members across all offices.
In collaboration with corporate services managers, monitors service delivery and identifies and implements improvements to ensure consistent client service experiences across offices.
Manages relationships with external agents, government bodies, and service providers.
In collaboration with Knowledge & Practice Support, coordinates implementation of legislative and regulatory changes impacting corporate services.
Prepares reports and presentations and participates in strategic projects.
Fosters a collaborative and high-performing team culture.

Qualifications

University or College degree in a related discipline; Law Clerk or Paralegal diploma is an asset.
Minimum of 12 years of work experience in corporate law or corporate services, including at least 8 years in progressive leadership roles.
Strong understanding of corporate services processes and regulatory requirements across Canadian jurisdictions.
Experience leading national teams, process harmonization, and change initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into operational execution.
Strong technology aptitude: experience with entity management systems (e.g., Athennian, Minutebox, ALF, Enact) is an asset.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, and project management abilities.
Client‑focused mindset with a collaborative leadership style.
Bilingualism (French/English) is an asset.

Benefits/Perks

Gowling WLG’s total rewards program is designed to foster a culture where high performance and personal well-being go hand-in-hand. We support your career and life with:

100% employer-paid health, dental, and mental health coverage, plus an annual lifestyle spending allowance
Benefits coverage for Firm members and their dependents from day one!
20+ vacation days and hybrid work flexibility
Parental leave top-up for 26 weeks (after 12 months of full-time employment)
Group Retirement Savings Plan with employer match
Financial protection through short & long-term disability, life, accident & critical illness insurance
Employee & Family Assistance Program, guided CBT, and an internal network of 120+ trained Mental Health First Aid responders
Recognition awards, appreciation events, and a supportive, collaborative work culture
Perks and preferred pricing programs, referral bonuses and more

This position is currently vacant and is open to both internal and external candidates. Gowling WLG is recruiting for this role to support ongoing firm needs and team operations.

This employer may use tools within our applicant tracking system that include artificial intelligence–supported features, such as automated candidate matching. These tools do not make hiring decisions; all screening, assessments, and selections are reviewed and completed by human recruiters and hiring managers.

Gowling WLG is dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. If you are in need of accommodation or support at any time during the recruitment process, please let us know.

The target base compensation for this role is $160,000 to $200,000 plus eligibility for bonus and other total rewards programs. For candidates with extensive and directly relevant experience, compensation may exceed the posted range.

new_jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
new_jobs.description:
At Equitable, we believe work should be a place where you feel supported, inspired, and empowered to grow. In our caring and collaborative environment, your curiosity is encouraged, your passion is recognized, and your contributions truly matter. Together, we create meaningful impact, for our clients, our communities, and each other.

The Opportunity:
  At Equitable, we believe great things happen when we work together. We’re a Canadian mutual company driven by purpose - putting people first and helping Canadians protect today and prepare for tomorrow. If you’re passionate about making a difference and growing your career in an inclusive and collaborative environment, we’d love to hear from you.

Our culture is built on care, passion and curiosity. We put people above all else, strive to be our best and welcome new ideas to deliver positive outcomes.

As Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), you’ll provide strategic and operational leadership for Equitable’s enterprise information security program, protecting our information assets, technology infrastructure, applications, data, and digital capabilities while enabling business growth and innovation. You’ll define and execute our cyber security strategy, ensuring effective security controls, processes, and practices are embedded across technology and business operations. Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer, you’ll lead the continued development of a resilient, risk-aware security culture while ensuring compliance with applicable legislation, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and recognized security frameworks.

Join one of the region’s top employers and be part of something that truly makes a difference.

Work Arrangements:
This is a hybrid role. You will work in our office in Waterloo, ON a minimum of two (2) assigned, consecutive days every other week, plus a fifth (5th) assigned day per month. You are welcome to work from the office more than the minimum requirement and there may be some roles that are required to work in our office more than the minimum requirement.

Reports To:
Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer

Department:
Information Technology

Term:
Permanent Full-Time

What you’ll do:

Serve as a senior technology leader and trusted advisor to the Executive Vice President, Chief Information Officer and Executive Team on cyber security, significant incidents, emerging threats, vulnerabilities, and security program developments
Develop and execute the enterprise cyber security strategy, roadmap, budget, and investment priorities aligned with business and technology objectives, including anticipating and mitigating risks associated with AI-enabled threats and vulnerabilities
Establish and maintain information security policies, standards, procedures, controls, metrics, and performance indicators, driving continuous improvement in the organization’s security capabilities and maturity
Lead security operations, threat monitoring, vulnerability management, cyber resilience, incident response, recovery, post-incident remediation, and the oversight of security service providers and critical technology assets
Oversee security architecture, identity and access management, data protection, cloud and endpoint security, ensuring appropriate controls are integrated into technology solutions, projects, and business processes
Partner with business and technology leaders to enable secure innovation and digital transformation, provide security guidance for strategic initiatives and new capabilities, and support operational resilience and business continuity
Lead security awareness and training across the organization, promoting a security-first mindset and fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, resilience, and risk awareness
Manage technology vendor and third-party security assessments while maintaining effective relationships with security vendors, managed security service providers, industry and regulatory bodies, external advisors, and peer security leaders within the financial services industry

What you’ll bring:

Deep technical knowledge of enterprise security architecture, including zero trust, network segmentation, secure-by-design principles, defence-in-depth, secure software development, DevSecOps, application security testing, and API security
Strong understanding of hybrid and multi-cloud environments, cloud security posture management, and security across SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS platforms, with the ability to assess the security implications of core insurance and wealth platforms, legacy systems, and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled solutions
Extensive experience with SIEM, endpoint detection and response, and 24x7 security monitoring models, including managed security service providers, along with vulnerability and patch management, threat intelligence, penetration testing, and red/purple team practices
Proven ability to lead cyber incident response, crisis management, forensics, and recovery activities, including ransomware and third-party breach scenarios, with a strong understanding of disaster recovery, backup integrity, and operational resilience for critical business services
Deep knowledge of identity governance, privileged access management, multifactor authentication, single sign-on, conditional access, identity lifecycle controls, access certification, segregation of duties, and least-privilege enforcement across cloud and legacy environments
Strong knowledge of data discovery and classification, data loss prevention, encryption in transit and at rest, and cryptographic key, certificate, and secrets management, including controls protecting sensitive information shared with third parties or used by AI-enabled solutions
Demonstrated ability to challenge security designs and assessment findings, validate control effectiveness through technical evidence, and prioritize remediation based on exploitability, risk, and business impact
Experience evaluating security technologies and service providers for effectiveness, integration, operational complexity, and total cost of ownership, with the ability to translate technical gaps into prioritized security roadmaps with measurable outcomes, funding requirements, and the skills and resources required for delivery

What’s in it for you:

Career Growth: Regular learning sessions and development opportunities 
Total Rewards: Incentive pay, annual salary reviews, employer-paid benefits and pension matching 
Time Away: Competitive vacation plus one paid volunteer day each year
Flexibility: Healthy work-life balance with employee wellness always top of mind, complemented by a “dress for your day” approach

We’re committed to fair pay and an inclusive, accessible hiring experience. If you need accommodations or alternative formats at any stage, just reach out to us at careers@equitable.ca. We’re happy to help.

If you’re selected to move forward, our Talent Acquisition team will walk you through all the details of our total rewards program, so you know exactly what’s included. This position is open and we are excited to find the right person to join our team. Your base pay will be based on your skills, qualifications, experience and education.

At Equitable, your resume will be reviewed by real people and all hiring decisions are made by our recruiters and hiring managers. AI tools may be used to support administrative and productivity tasks throughout the recruitment process, but we believe that evaluating experience, skills, and talent potential requires meaningful human interaction.

As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure and trusted workplace, candidates selected to move forward in the recruitment process will be required to complete a background screening in accordance with company policy.

new_jobs.description:
About Gowling Wlg

At Gowling WLG, our commitment to excellence begins with our people. As an international law firm with offices in Canada, the U.K., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, we’re proud to recruit and retain top talent who bring energy, insight, and a singular focus on delivering exceptional experiences – for our clients and each other.

We’re intentional about building a workplace that’s both high-performing and supportive, ensuring that everyone is empowered to do their best work and reach their full potential. Our culture is grounded in our shared values: Raise the Bar, Embrace Differences, and Thrive Together. These values shape how we collaborate, lead, and succeed – across teams, time zones, and career paths.

Whether you’re pursuing a role in law or business services, explore what’s possible and make your mark with Gowling WLG.

PROFILE

The Director, Corporate Services is a senior leadership role responsible for overseeing the delivery of corporate services across all Gowling WLG offices nationally. This role provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure consistent, high‑quality, and efficient support for the Firm’s Corporate professionals and clients. You will lead national teams, drive process standardization, oversee enabling technologies, and partner with key stakeholders to continuously improve service delivery, client experience, and operational performance.

This position can be based in our Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Hamilton, Waterloo or Ottawa office.

Responsibilities

Directs the efforts of the national Corporate Services team, including the development and implementation of strategies aligned with the Firm’s business goals to enhance corporate services delivery in all provinces in which the Firm operates.
Directs and enables development of an integrated team culture, vision and mission that drives effective interoffice collaboration, resource allocation and work sharing.
Ensures consistent application of standardized workflows, procedures, and precedents across all jurisdictions which the Firm operates, and subject to local requirements.
Provides senior oversight and strategic guidance on the selection, configuration and ongoing operation of corporate services technology platforms.
Partners with IT, Innovation, Knowledge & Practice Support, Finance, and Corporate leadership on technology, automation, precedents, and process improvement initiatives.
Responsible for ensuring effective and consistent onboarding, training, and continuous development programs for Corporate Services team members across all offices.
In collaboration with corporate services managers, monitors service delivery and identifies and implements improvements to ensure consistent client service experiences across offices.
Manages relationships with external agents, government bodies, and service providers.
In collaboration with Knowledge & Practice Support, coordinates implementation of legislative and regulatory changes impacting corporate services.
Prepares reports and presentations and participates in strategic projects.
Fosters a collaborative and high-performing team culture.

Qualifications

University or College degree in a related discipline; Law Clerk or Paralegal diploma is an asset.
Minimum of 12 years of work experience in corporate law or corporate services, including at least 8 years in progressive leadership roles.
Strong understanding of corporate services processes and regulatory requirements across Canadian jurisdictions.
Experience leading national teams, process harmonization, and change initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into operational execution.
Strong technology aptitude: experience with entity management systems (e.g., Athennian, Minutebox, ALF, Enact) is an asset.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong organizational, analytical, and project management abilities.
Client‑focused mindset with a collaborative leadership style.
Bilingualism (French/English) is an asset.

Benefits/Perks

Gowling WLG’s total rewards program is designed to foster a culture where high performance and personal well-being go hand-in-hand. We support your career and life with:

100% employer-paid health, dental, and mental health coverage, plus an annual lifestyle spending allowance
Benefits coverage for Firm members and their dependents from day one!
20+ vacation days and hybrid work flexibility
Parental leave top-up for 26 weeks (after 12 months of full-time employment)
Group Retirement Savings Plan with employer match
Financial protection through short & long-term disability, life, accident & critical illness insurance
Employee & Family Assistance Program, guided CBT, and an internal network of 120+ trained Mental Health First Aid responders
Recognition awards, appreciation events, and a supportive, collaborative work culture
Perks and preferred pricing programs, referral bonuses and more

This position is currently vacant and is open to both internal and external candidates. Gowling WLG is recruiting for this role to support ongoing firm needs and team operations.

This employer may use tools within our applicant tracking system that include artificial intelligence–supported features, such as automated candidate matching. These tools do not make hiring decisions; all screening, assessments, and selections are reviewed and completed by human recruiters and hiring managers.

Gowling WLG is dedicated to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. If you are in need of accommodation or support at any time during the recruitment process, please let us know.

The target base compensation for this role is $160,000 to $200,000 plus eligibility for bonus and other total rewards programs. For candidates with extensive and directly relevant experience, compensation may exceed the posted range.
